sections.text:
تستخدم هذه الطريقة لتعيين كثافة المنتجات البترولية عند درجة حرارة قياسية 
 معينة (غالبا ما تكون 15م 
 او 20م 
 مع العلم انه يمكن تقدير هذه الكثافة عند درجة حرارة اخرى ثم يتم تصحيح القيمة 
 بالنسبة لدرجة الحرارة القياسية حسابيا.

قام بإعداد هذا المستند الكيميائية/ 
 غادة سليمان احمد محمد وتم مراجعة المستند 
 بمعرفة الكيميائي/
 عبد الناصر محمد الأمين وقام بالاختبار السيد الكيميائي/ 
 اشرف صلاح الدين صالح وتم اعتماده من الكيميائى/ 
 محمد وجدى عبد الله 
 مدير عام بمحطة كهرباء السد العالى بشركة 
 المحطات المائية لإنتاج الكهرباء وموثق من المهندس/ 
 عبد النبى عبد الغنى عبد النبى 
 رئيس قطاع المحطة بشركة 
 المحطات المائية 
 لإنتاج الكهرباء.

وهذا المستند معتمد من المهندس/ 
 محمد اسامة سليمان سليم منسق الـMPIS بشركة 
 المحطات المائية لإنتاج الكهرباء.

rows:
تعتبر هذه الطريقة هى الانسب 
 لتعيين كثافة منتجات البترول السائلة الشفافة 
 .

ضع جزء من العينة 
 فى مخبار الكثافة ثم اغمس فية ترمومتر وتأكد من درجة حرارة 
 كلا من العينة والمخبار هى نفس درجة الحرارة القياسية المطلوب تعيين 
 الكثافة عندها (يتم تجديد هذه الدرجة طبقا للمواصفات التى يخضع لها السائل).

اختار الهيدروميتر المناسب لهذه الطريقة اغمسه فى 
 العينة واتركة ليستقر معلقا فى العينة.

عند درجة الحرارة 
 القياسية يتم اخذ قراءة الهيدروميتر.

اذا كانت درجة الحرارة القياسية ليست درجة الحرارة 
 المراد قياس كثافة العينة عندها فانه يمكن تصحيح قيمة الكثافة حسابيا.

هى كتلة وحدة الحجوم من السائل عند درجة الحرارة القياسية (15م˚، 
 20م˚)
 وحدة قياس الكثافة هى كجم/ م3 
 (kg/m3)
الكثافة

يتم اخذ العينة بالطريقة السليمة السالف ذكرها طبقا للـ 
 (MPIS(Oil-013-r2.

تأكد من صحة البيانات الواردة 
 على العينة.

التأكد من وضع 
 العينة فى الصندوق الخاص بها لعدم تعرضها لضوء اشمس والاتربة .
التأكد من ان زجاجة العينة جافة (خالية من المياه والاتربة).
عند اجراء الاختبار تجنب انسكاب الزيت على الارض واذا حدث ذلك يتم ازالته.

هيدرومترات زجاجية مدرجة بوحدات كثافة مطابقة لمواصفة 
 IEC 296-82 .

ترمومترات لها مدى تدريجى 
 واضح (نسبة خطأ فى الحدود المسموح بها).

حمام مائى له 
 درجة حرارة ثابتة (ان وجد) يمكنه احتواء مخبار الهيدروميتر المحتوى على 
 الهيدروميتر والعينة معدل التغير فى درجة حرارة 
 الحمام المائى لا يزيد عن 0.25 م˚ 
 عن الدرجة القياسية.

انقل العينة الى مخبار نظيف يكون قطرة الداخلى يزيد بمقدار 25 مم على القطر 
 الخارجى للهيدروميتر وذلك دون سكب اى قطرات من العينة لتفادى تكون فقعات 
 هواء.

تخلص من اى فقاعات هوائية متكونة على الاسطح بمسها خفيفا بواسطة ورقة ترشيح 
 وهذا قبل غمس الهيدروميتر.

تأكد من ان 
 المخبار فى وضع راسى تماما بعيدا عن التيارات الهوائية مع مراعاة الا تتغير 
 درجة الحرارة المحيطة بأكثر من 2م˚خلال 
 فترة الاختبار كاملا وفى حالة عدم مراعاة ذلك استخدم حمام مائى يحافظ على 
 درجة حرارة المخبار طوال فترة الاختبار.

اغمس الترمومتر 
 المناسب وقلب العينة مستعينا بساق فى حركة راسية دائرية لضمان ثبات توزيع 
 درجة الحرارة ثم سجل درجة حرارة العينة لأقرب 0.1 م˚ 
 ثم انزع الترمومتر وساق الثقليب من المخبار.

ملحوطة: عند استخدام الترمومتر كوسيلة لقياس 
 درجة الحرارة فأنه يمكن استخدامه كساق تقليب ايضا.

ضع الهيدروميتر المناسب فى العينة على ان تكون المسافة 
 بين نهاية الهيدروميتر وقاع المخبار 25 مم واتركة لمدة مناسبة ليستقر 
 ولتخرج فقاعات الهواء الى السطح ويتم التخلص منها قبل اخذ اى قراءة 
 للهيدروميتر, عند استقرار الهيدروميتر حرا فى 
 العينة بعيدا عن جدران المخبار سجل قراءة الهيدروميتر لاقرب 0.2.

يتم تسجيل قراءة الهيدروميتر من نقطة التقاء عين الرائى 
 مع مستوى سطح السائل على تدريج الهيدروميتر كما هو موضح فى الشكل المرفق.

اغمس الترمومتر 
 مرة اخرى فى المخبار وقلب راسيا ثم ارفع الهيدروميتر من العينة وسجل درجة 
 الحرارة لاقرب 0.1 م˚ 
 فى حالة اختلاف درجة الحرارة المقاسة عن تلك المقاسة سابقا باكثر من 0.5م˚ 
 فأنه يجب اعادة ضبط درجة الحرارة لأقرب 0.5م˚ 
 واذا لم يتسنى ذلك فيجب استخدام حمام مائى له درجة حرارة ثابتة وكرر عملية 
 القياس بنفس الطريقة مرة اخرى

ملحوظة: الكثافة 
 المقاسة ادق ما تكون كما كانت درجة حرارة القياس اقرب ما تكون للدرجة 
 القياسية.

صحح قيم درجة الحرارة للترمومتر المستخدم وقرب بين القرائتين 
 لأقرب 0.1 م˚.
صحح قيم قراءة تدريج الهيدروميتر المستخدم لأقرب 0.1 كجم/م3.

فى حالة عدم ضبط درجة الحرارة عند القياس لأقرب 0.5م˚ 
 فأنه يتم تصحيح قيمة الكثافة من خلال العلاقة التالية
 r20 
 = rT 
 {1+X(T-20} 
 حيث
 r20 
 الكثافة عند 20م˚ 
 (بفرض ان درجة الحرارة القياسية لهذا السائل 20م˚)
 rT 
 الكثافة المقاسة عند T
 X 
 (معامل التصحيح) = a10-5.65

Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: Oil-019-r0a
Equipment: Standard test method for density of liquid petroleum products by hydrometer method
Issued to: High Dam Power Station
Document Status: Approved
Document Approval Date: 20 January 2009
Procedure: IEC 269-82, IP 160-68, ASTM D1298-67
Date of Next Review: January 2014

sections_en.text: This method is used to determine the density of petroleum products at a specific standard temperature (usually 15°C or 20°C), noting that this density can be estimated at another temperature and the value then corrected to the standard temperature by calculation.

This document was prepared by the chemist Ghada Soliman Ahmed Mohamed, reviewed by the chemist Abdel Nasser Mohamed El-Amin, tested by the chemist Ashraf Salah El-Din Saleh, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.

rows: This method is the most suitable for determining the density of transparent liquid petroleum products.

Place part of the sample in the density cylinder, immerse a thermometer in it, and make sure that the temperature of both the sample and the cylinder is the standard temperature at which the density is to be determined (this temperature is specified according to the specifications to which the liquid is subject).
Select the hydrometer suitable for this method, immerse it in the sample and leave it to settle, floating in the sample.
At the standard temperature, take the hydrometer reading.
If the standard temperature is not the temperature at which the sample density is to be measured, the density value can be corrected by calculation.
It is the mass of a unit volume of the liquid at the standard temperature (15°C, 20°C); the unit of density is kg/m³ (kg/m3).
Density
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2).
Make sure the data on the sample are correct.
Make sure the sample is placed in its own box so that it is not exposed to sunlight and dust.
Make sure the sample bottle is dry (free of water and dust).
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor; if this happens, remove it.
Glass hydrometers graduated in density units, conforming to specification IEC 296-82.
Thermometers with a clear graduation range (error within the permissible limits).

A water bath with a constant temperature (if available) that can hold the hydrometer cylinder containing the hydrometer and the sample; the rate of change of the water bath temperature does not exceed 0.25°C from the standard temperature.
Transfer the sample to a clean cylinder whose inside diameter is 25 mm larger than the outside diameter of the hydrometer, without spilling any drops of the sample, to avoid forming air bubbles.
Remove any air bubbles formed on the surfaces by lightly touching them with filter paper, before immersing the hydrometer.

Make sure the cylinder is in a completely vertical position, away from air currents, taking care that the ambient temperature does not change by more than 2°C during the whole test period; if this is not observed, use a water bath that maintains the cylinder temperature throughout the test period.

Immerse the suitable thermometer and stir the sample with a rod in a vertical circular motion to ensure a stable temperature distribution, then record the sample temperature to the nearest 0.1°C, then remove the thermometer and the stirring rod from the cylinder.
Note: when the thermometer is used as a means of measuring temperature, it can also be used as a stirring rod.

Place the suitable hydrometer in the sample so that the distance between the end of the hydrometer and the bottom of the cylinder is 25 mm, and leave it for a suitable time to settle and for air bubbles to rise to the surface and be removed before taking any hydrometer reading. When the hydrometer is floating freely in the sample, away from the cylinder walls, record the hydrometer reading to the nearest 0.2.
The hydrometer reading is recorded from the point where the observer eye meets the liquid surface level on the hydrometer scale, as shown in the attached figure.

Immerse the thermometer again in the cylinder, stir vertically, then lift the hydrometer out of the sample and record the temperature to the nearest 0.1°C. If the measured temperature differs from that measured previously by more than 0.5°C, the temperature must be readjusted to the nearest 0.5°C; if this is not possible, use a water bath with a constant temperature and repeat the measurement in the same way again.
Note: the measured density is most accurate when the measurement temperature is closest to the standard temperature.
Correct the temperature values for the thermometer used and average the two readings to the nearest 0.1°C.
Correct the reading values of the hydrometer scale used to the nearest 0.1 kg/m³.

If the temperature at measurement is not adjusted to the nearest 0.5°C, the density value is corrected using the following relation: r20 = rT {1 + X(T - 20)} where r20 is the density at 20°C (assuming the standard temperature for this liquid is 20°C), rT is the density measured at T, and X (the correction factor) = a × 10⁻⁵·65.

rows: Repeatability: the difference between two results for the same person, the same apparatus, the same operating conditions and the same material at the same temperature is 0.5 kg/m³.
Reproducibility: the difference between two results for two different persons for the same sample at the same temperature is 1.2 kg/m³.

Maintenance Procedures Information System
 | Substations | Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: Oil-019-r0a | Equipment: Standard test method for density of liquid petroleum products by hydrometer method
Issued to: High Dam Power Station
Document Status: Approved
Document Approval Date: 20 January 2009 | Procedure: IEC 269-82, IP 160-68, ASTM D1298-67
Date of Next Review: January 2014
Introduction
This method is used to determine the density of petroleum products at a specific standard temperature (usually 15°C or 20°C), noting that this density can be estimated at another temperature and the value then corrected to the standard temperature by calculation.
This document was prepared by the chemist Ghada Soliman Ahmed Mohamed, reviewed by the chemist Abdel Nasser Mohamed El-Amin, tested by the chemist Ashraf Salah El-Din Saleh, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
Objective
This method is the most suitable for determining the density of transparent liquid petroleum products.
Summary of Method
Place part of the sample in the density cylinder, immerse a thermometer in it, and make sure that the temperature of both the sample and the cylinder is the standard temperature at which the density is to be determined (this temperature is specified according to the specifications to which the liquid is subject). | 
Select the hydrometer suitable for this method, immerse it in the sample and leave it to settle, floating in the sample. | 
At the standard temperature, take the hydrometer reading. | 
If the standard temperature is not the temperature at which the sample density is to be measured, the density value can be corrected by calculation. | 
Definition
It is the mass of a unit volume of the liquid at the standard temperature (15°C, 20°C); the unit of density is kg/m³ (kg/m3). | Density
Procedures Required for Measurement Accuracy
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2). | 
Make sure the data on the sample are correct. | 
Make sure the sample is placed in its own box so that it is not exposed to sunlight and dust. | 
Make sure the sample bottle is dry (free of water and dust). | 
Environmental Recommendations
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor; if this happens, remove it. | 1.
Tools and Apparatus
Glass hydrometers graduated in density units, conforming to specification IEC 296-82. | 1.
Thermometers with a clear graduation range (error within the permissible limits). | 2.
A water bath with a constant temperature (if available) that can hold the hydrometer cylinder containing the hydrometer and the sample; the rate of change of the water bath temperature does not exceed 0.25°C from the standard temperature. | 3.
Procedures to be Carried Out
Test Steps
Transfer the sample to a clean cylinder whose inside diameter is 25 mm larger than the outside diameter of the hydrometer, without spilling any drops of the sample, to avoid forming air bubbles. | 1.
Remove any air bubbles formed on the surfaces by lightly touching them with filter paper, before immersing the hydrometer. | 2.
Make sure the cylinder is in a completely vertical position, away from air currents, taking care that the ambient temperature does not change by more than 2°C during the whole test period; if this is not observed, use a water bath that maintains the cylinder temperature throughout the test period. | 3.
Immerse the suitable thermometer and stir the sample with a rod in a vertical circular motion to ensure a stable temperature distribution, then record the sample temperature to the nearest 0.1°C, then remove the thermometer and the stirring rod from the cylinder. | 4.
Note: when the thermometer is used as a means of measuring temperature, it can also be used as a stirring rod.
Place the suitable hydrometer in the sample so that the distance between the end of the hydrometer and the bottom of the cylinder is 25 mm, and leave it for a suitable time to settle and for air bubbles to rise to the surface and be removed before taking any hydrometer reading. When the hydrometer is floating freely in the sample, away from the cylinder walls, record the hydrometer reading to the nearest 0.2. | 5.
The hydrometer reading is recorded from the point where the observer eye meets the liquid surface level on the hydrometer scale, as shown in the attached figure. | 6.
Immerse the thermometer again in the cylinder, stir vertically, then lift the hydrometer out of the sample and record the temperature to the nearest 0.1°C. If the measured temperature differs from that measured previously by more than 0.5°C, the temperature must be readjusted to the nearest 0.5°C; if this is not possible, use a water bath with a constant temperature and repeat the measurement in the same way again. | 7.
Note: the measured density is most accurate when the measurement temperature is closest to the standard temperature.
Calculations
Correct the temperature values for the thermometer used and average the two readings to the nearest 0.1°C. | 1.
Correct the reading values of the hydrometer scale used to the nearest 0.1 kg/m³. | 2.
If the temperature at measurement is not adjusted to the nearest 0.5°C, the density value is corrected using the following relation: r20 = rT {1 + X(T - 20)} where r20 is the density at 20°C (assuming the standard temperature for this liquid is 20°C), rT is the density measured at T, and X (the correction factor) = a × 10⁻⁵·65. | 
Precision: Precision is subject to laboratory results as follows:
Repeatability: the difference between two results for the same person, the same apparatus, the same operating conditions and the same material at the same temperature is 0.5 kg/m³. | 1.
Reproducibility: the difference between two results for two different persons for the same sample at the same temperature is 1.2 kg/m³. | 2.
